question: A 60-year-old man comes to the office because of an 8-month history of cough, night sweats, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has also had a 9-kg (19.8-lb) weight loss during this time. He appears pale. Abdominal examination shows hepatosplenomegaly. His leukocyte count is 80,000/mm3 and his leukocyte alkaline phosphatase level is increased. A peripheral blood smear shows > 82% neutrophils with band forms and immature and mature neutrophil precursors. An x-ray of the chest shows a 9-mm right hilar nodule. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's laboratory findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Tuberculosis -> Granulomatous inflammation -> Hepatosplenomegaly -> Night sweats, weight loss, fatigue -> Cough, shortness of breath -> Increased leukocyte count, leukocyte alkaline phosphatase -> Neutrophilia with band forms and immature neutrophil precursors -> Right hilar nodule on chest x-ray -> 80%

CHAIN: Leukemoid reaction -> Increased leukocyte count -> Increased leukocyte alkaline phosphatase -> Neutrophilia with band forms and immature neutrophil precursors -> Hepatosplenomegaly -> Night sweats, weight loss, fatigue -> Cough, shortness of breath -> Right hilar nodule on chest x-ray -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation with cough, night sweats, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, leukocytosis with increased leukocyte alkaline phosphatase, and a chest x-ray showing a hilar nodule is highly suggestive of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). The peripheral blood smear findings of >82% neutrophils with immature forms further support this diagnosis.
